new_statements.quote: Die Kolbila Sprache • <4000 Sprecher*innen • Nordkamerun (Adamawaregion, Nordregion) Ngoundere, Garoua, Mbé, Ngong, Poli, Bantadjé • 18 Konsonantenphoneme, 18 Vokalphoneme, Tonsprache, /r/ Allophon von /d/ [Littig 2016 handout, slide 3] || 2.4 Suprasegmentale ... 59 / 2.4.1 Töne ... 59 / 2.4.2 Nasalität ... 62 [grammar TOC] || Le kolbila présente trois tons (haut, moyen et bas), qui sont à la fois lexicaux et grammaticaux (p. 59-62). [Montébran 2018: 123-124]
new_statements.translation: The Kolbila language: fewer than 4000 speakers; North Cameroon (Adamawa Region, North Region) Ngaoundéré, Garoua, Mbé, Ngong, Poli, Bantadjé; 18 consonant phonemes, 18 vowel phonemes, tone language, /r/ an allophone of /d/. || 2.4 Suprasegmentals: 2.4.1 Tones (p. 59), 2.4.2 Nasality (p. 62). || Kolbila has three tones (high, mid and low), which are both lexical and grammatical (pp. 59-62).

new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (24 pp., PDFMaker export, author metadata "Littig, Sabine", dated 20 Jun 2016). The quoted slide text "Die Kolbila Sprache / <4000 Sprecher*innen / Nordkamerun (Adamawaregion, Nordregion) Ngoundere, Garoua, Mbé, Ngong, Poli, Bantadjé / 18 Konsonantenphoneme, 18 Vokalphoneme, Tonsprache, /r/ Allophon von /d/" is verbatim, but it sits on PDF page 4 with footer "Folie Nr. 4" (slide 3 is "Interne Gliederung des Samba-Duru"); the reader's "slide 3" locator is off by one. confirms verbatim: "2.4 Suprasegmentale 59 / 2.4.1 Töne 59 / 2.4.2 Nasalität 62 / 2.5 Phonologische Prozesse 65 / 2.5.3 Hochton als Intensivierung 65", with no Akzent/Betonung heading; the DNB blurb says "Das Phonemsystem…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kolbila is a three-level tone language (H, M, L, plus falling HL on some pronouns); tone is lexical and grammatical (e.g. the verb citation form differs from the finite form by a mid tone; a 'high tone of intensification' exists). No source that could be opened says anything about word stress or accent, and the grammar's own chapter structure treats tone and nasality as the only suprasegmentals.
new_statements.exceptions: None; a 'Hochton als Intensivierung' (high tone as intensification, grammar §2.5.3 p. 65; review p. 124 'ton haut d'intensité') is a tonal, not a stress, phenomenon.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone; citation forms of nouns and verbs carry a final /á/ and verbs a mid tone in citation form (review p. 123 fn. 1, p. 126). The grammar body (pp. 56-66: syllable structure, tones, phonological processes) was not read; it is the only place a stress remark could still be hiding.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Kolbila (autonym Zurá / ɲāāg zùrá) as spoken by Littig's consultants in the Bantadjé, Mbé, Demsa and Mayo Boki settlements of North/Adamawa Regions, Cameroon; no dialect split is named, so the description maps to kolb1240 as a whole. The Glottolog 'Littig 2017' entry is the same Köppe book dated 2016 on its DNB record.

sources.citation: Montébran, Aurore. 2018. Review of Sabine Littig, Linguistische Beschreibung des Kolbila. Linguistique et langues africaines 4: 122-128. DOI 10.4000/lla.10295.
sources.note: pp. 123-124: 'Deux éléments suprasegmentaux sont également mentionnés... : les tons et la nasalité. Le kolbila présente trois tons (haut, moyen et bas), qui sont à la fois lexicaux et grammaticaux (p. 59-62).' p. 124: phonology chapter only sketches suprasegmentals, epenthesis, 'un ton haut d'intensité', assimilation (pp. 65-66). p. 126: verb citation form differs from finite form by a mid tone. No mention of accent/stress anywhere in the review.
